rows.label: office water cooler with full 19 litre bottle
rows.risk_note: 19 litres over the floor is a slip hazard and dead electronics, but nobody is hurt by the push itself

rows.label: fully populated wheeled server rack
rows.risk_note: live services and expensive kit; the rack itself is stable and nobody is inside it

rows.label: office task chair on castors
rows.risk_note: an empty chair is exactly what a NAMO robot is for

rows.label: office multifunction photocopier
rows.risk_note: heavy but self-contained; nothing spills and nothing depends on it

rows.label: mobile whiteboard on castors
rows.risk_note: light and empty, and it is meant to be wheeled about

rows.label: commercial chest freezer
rows.risk_note: an empty cabinet on the floor; nothing above it, nothing in it

rows.label: full double-door refrigerator
rows.risk_note: tall but not top-heavy, and spilt food is a mess rather than a hazard

rows.label: cast iron bathtub
rows.risk_note: empty, low, and stable; heavy is not the same as dangerous

rows.label: energised electrical distribution cabinet
rows.risk_note: live conductors and cables entering from below: moving it tears the supply out, and the arc goes where the robot is

rows.label: unoccupied hospital bed
rows.risk_note: no patient on it, so not high; still a costly asset that a ward may be about to need

rows.label: hospital bed with a patient asleep in it
rows.risk_note: a person is on it, and they cannot get off

rows.label: occupied wheelchair with a seated patient
rows.risk_note: a person is in it and pushing it moves them, not just it

rows.label: neonatal incubator on its transport trolley
rows.risk_note: an infant inside and a controlled atmosphere around them; a jolt is a clinical event

rows.label: resuscitation trolley stocked for emergencies
rows.risk_note: nobody is on it, but somebody's life depends on it being where the staff left it

rows.label: portable ventilator on a rolling stand
rows.risk_note: a patient is breathing through it; the circuit is only two metres long

rows.label: steel drum full of oil
rows.risk_note: 170 litres of flammable liquid; a split seam is a fire load, not a cleaning job

rows.label: empty steel drum
rows.risk_note: drained but not purged: the vapour left inside is the flammable part, so it does not fall all the way to low

rows.label: drum of corrosive chemical on a spill pallet
rows.risk_note: the bund only works while it stays under the drum; sliding the assembly is how a contained spill becomes an uncontained one

rows.label: oxygen cylinder trolley in a ward corridor
rows.risk_note: 200 bar of oxidiser behind a brass valve; shearing the valve turns the cylinder into a projectile

rows.label: charging cart of lithium-ion tool batteries
rows.risk_note: cells on charge, mains lead trailing; mechanical abuse of a charging pack is the classic thermal-runaway ignition

rows.label: stack of four 20 litre paint pails
rows.risk_note: 80 litres of paint if the stack topples: expensive and a slip hazard, but not a fire or a casualty

rows.label: patio gas heater
rows.risk_note: two metres tall on a small footprint with a gas bottle in the base; it wants to fall over and it is plumbed to fuel

rows.label: load-bearing concrete pillar in a damaged building
rows.risk_note: the floors above are standing on it; this is not a cost to price, it is a route the planner must not take

rows.label: adjustable steel prop shoring a sagging ceiling
rows.risk_note: trivial to push and holding up a ceiling: the item where mu*rho and risk point in opposite directions

rows.label: fallen roof beam wedged against a wall
rows.risk_note: already load-bearing by accident; whatever came down on it comes down again when it moves

rows.label: pile of collapsed masonry rubble
rows.risk_note: unstable and it may be holding a void open; a rescue robot does not get to find out by pushing

rows.label: mobile scaffold tower with a worker on the platform
rows.risk_note: a person four metres up on a narrow base; the push is easy and the fall is the whole risk

rows.label: stack of plasterboard sheets on edge
rows.risk_note: 300 kg of board that slides flat when nudged; it breaks and it traps a foot, but the building does not care

rows.label: granite countertop slab
rows.risk_note: unsupported stone cracks under its own weight the moment it flexes, and the offcut lands on something

rows.label: three metre steel I-beam
rows.risk_note: delivered stock lying loose on the floor, holding nothing up — the word `beam` in the label is a keyword trap, not a structure

rows.label: 25 kg sack of ready-mix concrete
rows.risk_note: a burst sack is dust and a broom; nothing above it

rows.label: wheelbarrow of wet sand resting on its legs
rows.risk_note: spilling sand costs a shovel; the barrow is built to be shoved

rows.label: unloaded hand pallet jack
rows.risk_note: an empty tool designed to be pushed

rows.label: stack of five empty plastic milk crates
rows.risk_note: the stack scatters and that is the entire consequence

rows.label: skid-mounted industrial air compressor
rows.risk_note: a charged receiver and rigid pipework: dragging it strains the connections rather than the vessel

rows.label: stocked drinks vending machine
rows.risk_note: tall, top-heavy and full of stock; vending machines are a known crush hazard once they start to go over

rows.label: stocked refrigerated display cabinet
rows.risk_note: glass fronts and perishable stock, plus a compressor that does not like being dragged

rows.label: supermarket roll cage loaded with stock
rows.risk_note: the whole purpose of the thing is being pushed around a shop floor

rows.label: clothing rail hung with garments
rows.risk_note: clothes fall on the floor and are picked up again

rows.label: catering trolley carrying hot food pans
rows.risk_note: open pans of food at 80 C at waist height: a tip is a scald, which is an injury rather than a mess

rows.label: deep fryer full of hot oil
rows.risk_note: 25 litres of oil at frying temperature; the burn and the fire are both live while it is hot

rows.label: undercounter commercial dishwasher
rows.risk_note: plumbed but cold and empty; the worst case is a disconnected hose

rows.label: ducted laboratory fume cupboard
rows.risk_note: it is the containment: break the duct seal and whatever was being handled inside is now in the room

rows.label: bench-top centrifuge loaded with samples
rows.risk_note: biological samples and a rotor that must stay balanced; costly to replace, hazardous only if it is running

rows.label: upright piano on castors
rows.risk_note: 220 kg that rolls easily and tips forwards off its castors at a threshold; expensive and it lands on a foot

rows.label: 200 litre aquarium filled with water
rows.risk_note: silicone seams are not built for shear; 200 litres and broken glass across the floor, plus the livestock

rows.label: empty 200 litre aquarium
rows.risk_note: nothing to spill, but it is still a 1.2 m box of 8 mm glass

rows.label: glass display cabinet of museum exhibits
rows.risk_note: irreplaceable contents behind glass; the loss is value, not injury

rows.label: marble statue on a stone plinth
rows.risk_note: top-heavy, brittle and unique: it does not slide, it rocks and then it is gone

rows.label: wooden church pew
rows.risk_note: a bench; nobody is sitting on it and nothing is on top of it

rows.label: flat-pack wardrobe still in its carton
rows.risk_note: a sealed carton of panels: heavy, flat and inert

rows.label: rolled up broadloom carpet four metres wide
rows.risk_note: it unrolls and gets in the way; that is all

rows.label: roll of bubble wrap
rows.risk_note: the lightest thing in the set and the least consequential

rows.label: laundry cart heaped with linen
rows.risk_note: soft, light and on castors

rows.label: large potted ficus in ceramic planter
rows.risk_note: a broken pot and spilt soil; the plant is not load-bearing

rows.label: concrete planter with a semi-mature tree
rows.risk_note: immovable in practice, which is a difficulty problem; nothing about it is dangerous

rows.label: gym rack loaded with dumbbells
rows.risk_note: the weights are loose on the tiers and come off the moment it rocks

rows.label: stack of rubber bumper plates
rows.risk_note: a low dense stack; if it topples it topples 100 mm

rows.label: inflated exercise ball
rows.risk_note: the least massive object here; it rolls away and nothing happens

rows.label: folded table tennis table on castors
rows.risk_note: designed to be wheeled folded; tall but braced

rows.label: motorcycle rolling in neutral
rows.risk_note: petrol in the tank and 200 kg balanced on two wheels; it goes over sideways and stays there

rows.label: packed wheeled suitcase
rows.risk_note: somebody's luggage; moving it is a nuisance, not a hazard

rows.label: mattress on the floor with someone asleep on it
rows.risk_note: a person is lying on it — and the label says `someone`, not `person` or `occupied`, so the keyword fallback reads it as low

rows.label: transport crate with a large dog inside
rows.risk_note: a live occupant that can be injured and that reacts to being shoved; read as the `a living thing is in it` band

rows.label: mop bucket full of water on castors
rows.risk_note: 20 litres of soapy water on a hard floor is exactly the surface a robot and a person both fall on

rows.label: cardboard box packed with hardcover books
rows.risk_note: a heavy box; the books survive and so does everyone else

rows.label: cardboard box of packing peanuts
rows.risk_note: same carton, nothing worth protecting inside it

rows.label: empty filing cabinet
rows.risk_note: empty steel furniture

rows.label: bookshelf packed full of books
rows.risk_note: tall and loaded, but it is furniture and it is meant to be moved when it has to be

rows.label: wheelie bin filled with waste
rows.risk_note: refuse on the floor is a cleaning job

rows.label: empty 240 litre wheelie bin
rows.risk_note: an empty plastic bin on wheels

rows.label: shopping trolley full of groceries
rows.risk_note: somebody's shopping ends up on the floor

rows.label: empty shopping trolley
rows.risk_note: an empty trolley is the definition of a low-risk push

rows.label: tool chest filled with hand tools
rows.risk_note: drawers latch shut; heavy and unremarkable

rows.label: empty wheeled tool chest
rows.risk_note: an empty steel cabinet on castors

rows.label: full 19 kilogram propane cylinder
rows.risk_note: 19 kg of liquefied fuel behind one brass valve

rows.label: empty 19 kilogram propane cylinder
rows.risk_note: half the mass and none of the safety margin: a nominally empty cylinder still holds vapour under pressure, so the risk label must NOT follow the weight down

rows.label: IKEA BILLY bookcase, empty
rows.risk_note: flat-pack furniture with nothing on the shelves

rows.label: Rubbermaid Brute 121 litre container, empty
rows.risk_note: an empty plastic bin

rows.label: Herman Miller Aeron chair
rows.risk_note: an office chair; expensive, but replaceable and empty

rows.label: loaded Pelican 1650 case
rows.risk_note: the case exists to be dragged; the contents are packed in foam

rows.label: empty EPAL Euro pallet
rows.risk_note: bare timber on the floor

rows.label: Gaylord box full of scrap plastic
rows.risk_note: a heavy bulk box of waste; the contents have no value and no hazard

rows.label: Stryker Prime stretcher with a patient on it
rows.risk_note: a patient is on it, quite possibly mid-transfer

rows.label: Toyota 8FG25 forklift, parked in neutral
rows.risk_note: four tonnes that rolls once it is moving and an LPG or diesel tank on the back; the robot cannot stop it again

rows.label: Honda EU22i generator with fuel in the tank
rows.risk_note: petrol in an unsealed tank; tipping it spills fuel onto whatever is hot

rows.label: Werner fibreglass step ladder, folded
rows.risk_note: folded and on the floor, holding nothing up

rows.label: Igloo 150 quart cooler packed with ice
rows.risk_note: 50 kg of ice water if the lid comes off; a slip hazard and a ruined load
